newsitem.title: CHINA: China Buddhists pray for peaceful HK handover.
newsitem.headline: China Buddhists pray for peaceful HK handover.

text.p: Buddhists chanted ancient scriptures in a Tibetan temple in China's capital on Sunday, not to attain salvation but to celebrate the return of Hong Kong to mainland rule.

About 50 Tibetan Buddhist monks clad in crimson and saffron robes sat crosslegged among acrid yak butter candles in Beijing's Yonghe Lama Temple to hold a special ceremony to pray for peace during the handover of the British colony at midnight (1600 GMT) on Monday.
"This prayer session is not based on religious tenets, it's especially to celebrate Hong Kong's return," Ah Badelafu, office director of the temple, told Reuters.

China's ruling Communist Party tries to keep a tight rein on religious services and is particularly keen to control Buddhists from its restive Tibet region, where deep religious sentiment has been a source of resistance against Beijing's rule.
While a handful of lay believers joined the monks in their two-hour prayer session, most temple-goers were simply looking for a way to spend a day off.
"We didn't know about the ceremony, we just came as tourists," said one elderly woman from the southern province of Guangdong that borders Hong Kong.

China has mobilised every sector of society to celebrate its resumption of sovereignty over Hong Kong after 156 years of colonial rule and is billing the handover as one of the most important events of the year, if not the century.

Tibet's spiritual leader the Dalai Lama, in exile since an abortive 1959 uprising against Chinese rule, on Saturday warned that Hong Kong could lose many fundamental freedoms after its handover to Beijing.

Beijing has pledged Hong Kong can maintain its freewheeling lifestyle for 50 years after the handover under an arrangement it calls "one country, two systems", an agreement the Dalai Lama said China would violate if that served its purposes.

The Dalai Lama, who won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1989 for his campaign for more autonomy for his Himalayan homeland, said human rights and democracy would be the first casualties of Hong Kong's reunification with the mainland.
Beijing regularly denounces the Dalai Lama as a separatist, accusing him of trying to use religion to split Tibet from the rest of China.
